rows.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
rows.claim: Al-Qadi argues that Arab experience let eloquent listeners recognize the Qur'an's extraordinary eloquence without a fresh trial; those less eloquent would see its inimitability even more readily.
rows.anchor: وعقد القاضي فصلاً (في اختصاص القرآن بمزية في رتبة الفصاحة خارجة عن العادة)

rows.speaker: بعض شيوخنا
rows.claim: Some of the author's teachers answered a Jewish denial of the Qur'an's distinctive merit by reciting Qur'anic passages whose eloquence is self-evident.
rows.anchor: وقد أورد بعض شيوخنا عند جحد بعض اليهود أن للقرآن مزية

rows.speaker: القاضي عبد الجبار
rows.claim: Al-Qadi chiefly refuted opponents' attacks on the Qur'an, esoteric readings that displaced its apparent meaning, alleged contradictions, and objections to repetition or prolixity.
rows.anchor: ثم كان أكثر ما تجرد له القاضي عبد الجبار: الرد على مطاعن المخالفين في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daily transition from bright duha to a still night does not suggest that heaven has abandoned earth; likewise, a pause after revelation does not mean God abandoned or hated Muhammad.
rows.anchor: الواو لافتة إلى صورة مادية وواقع حسي، يشهد به الناس تألق الضوء في ضحوة النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's waaw points to the witnessed setting star and its apparent luminous link between sky and earth; this makes the descent of revelation to Muhammad less strange or disputable.
rows.anchor: اللفت بالواو إلى ظاهرة كونية مشهودة، يراها الناس في النجم إذا هوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur'anic oaths perform their proper work of emphasis, affirmation, and solemnity.
rows.anchor: والقسم فيها جميعاً على وجهه من التأكيد والتقرير والإعظام

rows.speaker: المفسرون والبلاغيون
rows.claim: Exegetes and rhetoricians commonly say the oath-waaw magnifies what follows; the author questions this account because created things cannot be measured against the Creator's greatness.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك يدعو إلى مراجعة لما قنع به المفسرون والبلاغيون في تأويل هذه الواو بأنها لإعظام ما تلاها

rows.speaker: الفخر الرازي والنيسابورى والطبرسى والشيخ محمد عبده
rows.claim: The author says philosophical and ishari interpretations by these commentators make the oath-waaw carry meanings it cannot plausibly bear.
rows.anchor: وحمّلوا الآيات من التأويلات الفلسفية والإشارية - في مثل ما نقرأ في تفاسير الفخر الرازي والنبيسابورى والطبرسى والشيخ محمد عبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an points plainly to the benefits of night, day, sun, and moon without an oath, as in passages on light, rest, and reckoning.
rows.anchor: مع ملاحظة أن البيان القرآني يلفت إلى آيتى الليل والنهار، أو الشمس والقمر، بغير القسم

words: إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوَى الْأَنْفُسُ
rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani says ellipsis can be more eloquent than stating the answer because the reader's mind can supply many possibilities; he illustrates with omitted conclusions in two Qur'anic passages.
rows.anchor: واستطرد الرماني إلى بيان وجه الإعجاز بإيجاز القصر في قوله تعالى:

words: إِنْ يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا الظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهْوَى الْأَنْفُسُ
rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani distinguishes concision without ellipsis from deletion, calling it subtler because one must know where deletion is suitable; he lists this phrase among examples of concise expression.
rows.anchor: واستطرد الرماني إلى بيان وجه الإعجاز بإيجاز القصر في قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Comparing the Qur'anic phrase with the maxim killing is the best deterrent to killing, al-Rummani says it conveys more: justice, the desired end of life, and appeal to desire and fear under God's law.
rows.anchor: واستطرد الرماني إلى بيان وجه الإعجاز بإيجاز القصر في قوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author notes that many descriptions of Resurrection use passive past or present forms, dispensing with an explicit agent, including the trumpet and cosmic events.
rows.anchor: ومعها سائر آيات النفخ في الصور، وكلها مبنية للعل المجهول، الماضي منها والمضارع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another way the Qur'an omits the agent at the Resurrection is to attribute the event to the affected thing through a reflexive or figurative construction, as in the splitting moon and sky.
rows.anchor: وإما أن يستغنى البيان القرآني عن ذكر الفاعل في موقف الآخرة، بإسناده إلى غير فاعله، مطاوعة أو مجازاً

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Asked by Nafi ibn al-Azraq about dusur, Ibn Abbas says they are what secures the ship, adducing a poetic line about a boat with joined planks and dusur.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: الدسر الذي تُحرز به السفينة. وشاهده:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gloss 'what a ship is sewn with' needs clarification because the cited line does not say what the ship is sewn with; the word is unique in form and root in the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: وتفسير الدسر، بالذي تخرز به السفينة يحتاج إلى مزيد إيضاح لا يقدمه الشاهد

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra glosses dusur as ship nails and the bands or straps that hold the vessel together.
rows.anchor: ومعناها عند الفراء: مسامير السفن وشرُطُها التي تُشد بها

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains dusur as the ribs of the ship.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير البخاري، عن مجاهد: دسر، اضلاع السفينة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Mujahid via Ibn Abbas identifies the boards as the ship's planks and dusur as its crosspieces; Ibn Abbas also glosses them as nails.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: الألواح ألواح السفينة والدسر معاريضها التي تُشَدّ بها السفينة، وعنه أيضاً: المسامير

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib likewise defines dusur as nails, singular disar, and derives the root's basic sense from forceful driving or thrusting.
rows.anchor: وعند الراغب كذلك أن الدُسر في الآية، المسامير، الواحد: دِسَار، قال: وأصل الدَّسْرِ الدفع الشديد بقهر

rows.speaker: ابن الأثير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Athir reads dusur in Ali's saying as a nail; in Umar's saying, the verb dasara means forcefully pushing and pitching a camel down for slaughter.
rows.anchor: وكذلك فسرها "ابن الأثير" بالمسامير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author disagrees with al-Khattabi's method of testing Qur'anic expressions against Arabic eloquence transmitted in the compilation era; the Qur'an should be the sound standard for Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: غير أنا نختلف معه، من حيث المبدأ، في قبول عرض العبارات القرآنية على ما نقل عصر التدوين من فصيح كلام العرب

rows.speaker: الخطابي
rows.claim: Al-Khattabi refutes claims that Qur'anic expressions depart from accepted eloquent Arabic, then examines the conventions of poetic imitation and alleged imitations by false prophets, especially Musaylima's poor efforts.
rows.anchor: وتفرغ الخطابي في النصف الأخير من رسالته، لنقض ما سموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author values al-Khattabi's early rhetorical and critical discussion but says giving attention to later prophetic pretenders' feeble imitations grants them undeserved standing.
rows.anchor: ونرى مع ذلك أن أبا سليمان كان في غنى عن الاشتغال بهذيان من ادعوا النبوة بعد عصر الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reassurance that Muhammad is not mad answers the accusation in al-Hijr that called him mad because the Reminder had been sent down to him.
rows.anchor: رداً على ما في سورة أخرى

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan rejects treating la as a standalone answer, since that reading requires deleting both the noun and predicate of la, and the verse is not answering a question.
rows.anchor: ورَّده "أبو حيان" بأنه لا يجوز

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported reading takes la as an introductory particle that prepares for an omitted answer, reconstructed here as saying people will not be left purposeless.
rows.anchor: وقيل هي زائدة: توطئة وتمهيداً لنفي الجواب محذوفاً

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects positing an omitted answer because other la uqsim passages state their answers explicitly, including that God is able and that the Qur'an is noble.
rows.anchor: ورُد هذا التأويل بأنه لا وجه لتقدير جواب، والجواب صريح في مثل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says la is inserted merely to strengthen speech, with an alleged parallel in the verse about the People of the Book knowing God's bounty.
rows.anchor: وفي قول إنها زيدت لمجرد التأكيد وتقوية الكلام. ونظيره عندهم، آية الحديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author objects that an added particle is normally placed inside a clause, whereas its opening position gives it prominence and signals attention.
rows.anchor: ورُدّ بأنها لا تزاد لذلك في صدر الكلام، بل تزاد حشواً

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A third reading says la is the lām of initiation with its vowel lengthened into an alif, as in a poet's pronunciation of al-aqrab as al-aqrāb.
rows.anchor: وقول ثالث: إنها ليست نافية ولا زائدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if al-Zamakhshari's objection does not rule out a lengthened lām, the author finds that reading confusing because it can be mistaken for negative la.
rows.anchor: إذا لم يبعده رد "الزمخشري"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Across the Qur'an, every la uqsim oath uses the first-person speaker for God, a consistent stylistic pattern that informs the interpretation.
rows.anchor: فيهدينا إلى اطراد مجئ آيات "لا أقسم" وضمير المتكلم فيها، لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath verb elsewhere in the Qur'an is also ascribed to God without la; negative la with the oath verb is never used of another speaker, while prohibitive la in 24:53 is a separate construction.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاءت "لا" الناهية في آية النور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath does not invoke night and day in general but their perceptible contrast: darkness covering the world against the brightness of day, paralleled by the difference between male and female creation.
rows.anchor: وإذ لم يتعلق البيان القرآني فيهما بغير الغشية والتجلي، نلمح السر البياني فيما تلفت إليه الواو من تقابل واضح محسوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The visible contrasts of night and day and male and female prepare readers to grasp the moral and unseen contrasts that follow: giving and withholding, guidance and denial, ease and hardship, and the divergent afterlife outcomes.
rows.anchor: توطئة إيضاحية لبيان تفاوت مماثل في معنويات لا تدرك بالحس: {إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّى}

words: وَمَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُ مَالُهُۥٓ إِذَا تَرَدَّىٰٓ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses tarda as dying and falling into Hell; he cites a line by Adi ibn Zayd about a man struck by death while expecting a long reign.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: إذا مات وتردى في النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes al-mutardiya in 5:3 from Ibn Abbas's gloss: it refers to an animal killed by a fall, from a rock, mountain, or well; the root carries senses of death and destructive falling.
rows.anchor: واضح أن المتردية فيها بيست من الموت والتردى في النار، وإنما هي على أصل دلالتها في الهلاك بالمِرْداة، أي الصخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the Qur'an reserves emergence from graves for the Resurrection, as the contexts of its three occurrences make clear.
rows.anchor: يظهر، والله أعلم، أن القرآن خص الخروج من الأجداث بالمخرج يوم القيامة، وهو صريح السياق في آياتها الثلاث

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In the exchange with Nafi ibn al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas glosses halu'an as distressed and prone to lament, citing a line by Bishr ibn Abi Khazim.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: ضَجِراً جزوعاً. وشاهده قول بشر بن أبي خازم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra explains halu' as easily distressed and says the following verses define its behavior: panicking when harmed and withholding when favored.
rows.anchor: في معاني القرآن للفراء: الهلوع الضجور، وصفته كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: المعجميون
rows.claim: Lexicographers often narrow the word to extreme distress, with some restricting it to panic at misfortune and lack of patience in calamity.
rows.anchor: وخصها المعجميون بأفحش الجزع أو الجزع الشديد. وقيدها بعضهم بالجزع والفزع من الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author agrees with al-Farra and Tha'lab that the Qur'an itself explains halu' as panicking in adversity and withholding in prosperity.
rows.anchor: ونقول مع الفراء، وثعلب: وصفته كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: المعجميون
rows.claim: The lexicons also use related forms for a quick-moving ostrich, whose lightness makes it startle, and for a fast-moving she-camel.
rows.anchor: والهالع: النعام السريع في مضيه لخفته وسرعة فزعه. والهلواع: الناقة السريعة السير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says laata hina manas means that it is no longer a time to flee; the source introduces a supporting line by al-A'sha.
rows.anchor: قال: ليس بحين فرار. وشاهده قول الأعشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root's Qur'anic use occurs only as this imperfect verb in seven verses; ameh denotes bewilderment, transgression, heedlessness, and blindness of insight, near to literal blindness.
rows.anchor: وليس فى القرآن من المادة غير هذا الفعل المضارع فى الآيات السبع

rows.speaker: الخليل ويعقوب
rows.claim: Arabic calls a landmarkless area al-ard al-amha; the phrase for camels disappearing describes their vanishing when no one knows where they went.
rows.anchor: والأرض العمهاء فى العربية، التى لا أعلام فيها. وقالوا ذهبت إبلُه العُمَّهْى، حين لا يدرى أين ذهبت

rows.speaker: ابن الأثير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Athir compares spiritual bewilderment to physical blindness, saying it repeatedly occurs in hadith.
rows.anchor: والتفت "ابن الأثير " إلى صلة بين العمه والعمى

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda glosses ameh as deviating from the truth and cites Ru'ba's verse describing the ignorant as blind to guidance.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة فى (مجاز القرآن) : يقال

words: أَفَمَن يَمْشِى مُكِبًّا عَلَىٰ وَجْهِهِۦٓ أَهْدَىٰٓ
rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ibn Qutayba explains ya'mahoon as running headlong without seeing, and compares it to the person walking face down rather than upright on a straight path.
rows.anchor: وفى تأويل ابن قتيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author allows wandering or playing as a gloss for Lot's people in their intoxication, but says the other Qur'anic uses mean misguidance and blindness of insight.
rows.anchor: فتأويلها فى المسألة بالتردد واللعب، يُقبل فى آل لوط (فى سكرتهم يعمهون) لكنه فى سائر الآيات من الضلال وعمى البصيرة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari explains their ya'mah as bewildered error in transgression and disbelief, unable to find a way out.
rows.anchor: أو كما فى تأويل الطبرى: والعمَة نفسه: الضلال، يقال منه: عمِهَ عمها وعمهانا وعموها إذا ضل
